title: Listening — Practice test 2

parts.title: Part 1
parts.heading: Joining a sports centre
parts.context: A man is asking about membership at a sports centre.
script: Good afternoon, Greenfield Sports Centre. How can I help you?
Hello. I've just moved to the area and I'm interested in becoming a member. Could you tell me about the different types of membership?

Of course. We have three options. Standard membership gives you the gym and the pool. Plus membership includes all the classes as well, and Off-Peak is the same as Standard but only before four in the afternoon.
I work during the day, so Off-Peak wouldn't suit me. And I'm not really interested in classes. I'll go for Standard.
That's thirty-two pounds a month. There's also a joining fee of twenty pounds, but we're not charging it this month, so you won't have to pay that.
Great. Can I take your details, then?
Sure, let me take yours. What's your full name?
Daniel Ashworth. That's A, S, H, W, O, R, T, H.
Lovely. And what's your date of birth?
Thanks. Now, everyone who joins has to have a short induction with a trainer before using the gym. They're usually on Saturday mornings, but we also have them on Wednesday evenings.
OK. I'll put you down for this Saturday at ten o'clock. It takes about forty-five minutes. The trainer will show you how to use the equipment and ask about any injuries.
Actually, I hurt my knee last year playing football. It's much better now, though.
I'll make a note of that so the trainer knows. One more thing. You'll need to bring a photo for your membership card.
Do you mean a passport photo?
Any recent photo is fine, or we can take one here with a webcam if you prefer.
I'll bring one. And is there anywhere to leave my bike?
Yes, there's a bike rack behind the building, next to the tennis courts. The car park at the front is quite small, so most members cycle or walk.
That's perfect. Thank you very much.

parts.title: Part 2
parts.heading: Visiting Willow Marsh Nature Reserve
parts.context: A ranger is welcoming a group of visitors to a nature reserve.
script: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Willow Marsh Nature Reserve. My name's Tom, and I'm one of the rangers here. Before you set off, I'd like to give you some information about the reserve and what you can see today.

The reserve was created in 1985 on the site of an old gravel quarry. When the quarry closed, the pits filled with water, and the area was left alone for several years. Plants and birds gradually moved in, and local volunteers persuaded the council to protect it. Today it's managed by a charity, and it's still the volunteers who do most of the practical work.

Most people come here for the birds. In winter, the lakes are home to thousands of ducks and geese that fly here from northern Europe. At this time of year, in late spring, the most exciting visitors are probably the nightingales. You're unlikely to see one, because they hide in thick bushes, but you'll certainly hear them, especially early in the morning.

Please remember that dogs aren't allowed on the reserve, except for assistance dogs. We also ask you not to feed the birds. I know it's tempting, but bread is actually bad for them, and it pollutes the water.

If you're planning to walk all the way round, the main trail is about six kilometres and takes most people around two hours. It's flat, but some sections can be muddy after rain, so I'd recommend boots rather than trainers.
Now, let me tell you where to find things. Here at the visitor centre, we have toilets and a small shop, and you can borrow binoculars for free. Just leave some form of identification at the desk.
If you follow the trail to the north gate, you'll find the picnic area, with tables under the trees. There's also a children's play area right next to it.

The largest bird hide is beside the lake, about halfway round the trail. That's the best place to see kingfishers. Next to the hide there's a noticeboard where visitors write down the birds they've spotted that day.
And finally, if you'd like a hot drink when you get back, the café is here at the visitor centre. It closes at four, so don't be too late.

groups.instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

questions.text: What was the site of the reserve before 1985?
questions.evidence: on the site of an old gravel quarry
questions.explain_vi: 'an old gravel quarry' = mỏ sỏi cũ → B. Hồ hình thành SAU khi mỏ đóng cửa.

questions.text: Who does most of the practical work at the reserve today?
questions.evidence: it's still the volunteers who do most of the practical work
questions.explain_vi: Một tổ chức từ thiện quản lý, nhưng tình nguyện viên làm phần lớn công việc → A.

questions.text: What does the ranger say about nightingales?
options: They are easy to see in the bushes.
Visitors will probably hear them but not see them.
questions.evidence: You're unlikely to see one, because they hide in thick bushes, but you'll certainly hear them
questions.explain_vi: Khó nhìn thấy nhưng chắc chắn nghe được → C. Mùa đông là lúc vịt và ngỗng đến (B sai).

questions.text: Why should visitors not feed the birds?
questions.evidence: bread is actually bad for them, and it pollutes the water
questions.explain_vi: 'bread is actually bad for them' → A.

questions.text: What does the ranger recommend for walking the main trail?
questions.evidence: I'd recommend boots rather than trainers
questions.explain_vi: Đường có đoạn lầy sau mưa nên nên đi ủng → B.

groups.instructions: Where can visitors find each of the following? Choose A, B or C. You may use any letter more than once.

questions.text: binoculars to borrow
questions.evidence: you can borrow binoculars for free
questions.explain_vi: Mượn ống nhòm miễn phí ở trung tâm du khách → A.

questions.text: a children's play area
questions.evidence: There's also a children's play area right next to it.
questions.explain_vi: Khu vui chơi trẻ em ngay cạnh khu picnic ở cổng bắc → B.

questions.evidence: That's the best place to see kingfishers.
questions.explain_vi: Lều quan sát chim lớn nhất bên hồ là nơi tốt nhất để thấy chim bói cá → C.

questions.evidence: Next to the hide there's a noticeboard where visitors write down the birds they've spotted that day.
questions.explain_vi: Bảng tin cạnh lều quan sát (bên hồ) → C.

questions.evidence: the café is here at the visitor centre
questions.explain_vi: Quán café ở trung tâm du khách → A.

parts.title: Part 3
parts.heading: Preparing a presentation on urban gardens
parts.context: Two students, Clara and Ben, are talking to their tutor about a presentation.
script: So, Clara and Ben, how's the presentation on urban gardens coming along?
Quite well, I think. We've decided to focus on community gardens, the ones where local residents grow food together on shared land, rather than private gardens or rooftop farms.
That seems sensible. There's a lot of research on community gardens. What's your main argument going to be?

At first we wanted to show that they can feed a city, but the figures just don't support that. Even the biggest gardens produce only a small fraction of what people eat. So now we're arguing that their real value is social, bringing neighbours together.
Good, that's a much stronger position. How are you going to support it?
We've visited two gardens in the city and interviewed people there. The interviews were really useful, actually more useful than the questionnaire we sent out, because so few people returned it.
Twenty minutes, plus five minutes for questions. We were worried we'd have too little to say, but now we've got far too much, so we'll need to cut some sections.
That's a common problem. What do you think you'll cut?
Probably the history of community gardens. It's interesting, but it doesn't really support our argument.
I agree. Now, what about visuals?
We took lots of photos at the gardens. We were going to show a video too, but the sound quality was terrible, so we'll stick to photos and one or two simple charts.
Fine. Have you decided who's doing what?
Mostly. I'll do the introduction, because I'm more confident about speaking at the beginning.
And I'll present the interview results, since I did most of the interviews.
We'll prepare the slides together, so they look consistent.
Clara's going to contact the garden coordinators to ask permission to use their photos.
Ben's going to write that. He's better at summarising.
And we'll both answer questions at the end, depending on the topic.
That all sounds well organised. Good luck.

groups.instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

questions.text: What kind of gardens will the presentation focus on?
questions.evidence: We've decided to focus on community gardens
questions.explain_vi: Tập trung vào vườn cộng đồng, không phải vườn riêng hay nông trại trên mái → C.

questions.text: What is the students' main argument now?
options: Urban gardens can feed a city.
The main benefit of the gardens is social.
questions.evidence: So now we're arguing that their real value is social, bringing neighbours together.
questions.explain_vi: Ban đầu muốn chứng minh vườn nuôi được thành phố, nhưng số liệu không ủng hộ; nay lập luận giá trị là xã hội → B.

questions.text: Why were the interviews more useful than the questionnaire?
options: The questionnaire had poorly written questions.
The interviews were recorded on video.
questions.evidence: because so few people returned it
questions.explain_vi: Rất ít người gửi lại bảng hỏi → A.

questions.text: What problem do the students have with the presentation?
options: They have not finished the research.
questions.evidence: now we've got far too much, so we'll need to cut some sections
questions.explain_vi: Lúc đầu lo không đủ nội dung, giờ thì quá nhiều → B. Bẫy: A là nỗi lo ban đầu.

questions.text: Why will they not show a video?
questions.evidence: the sound quality was terrible
questions.explain_vi: 'the sound quality was terrible' → B.

groups.instructions: Who will do each task? Choose A, B or C. You may use any letter more than once.

questions.text: give the introduction
questions.evidence: I'll do the introduction
questions.explain_vi: Clara nói 'I'll do the introduction' → A.

questions.text: present the interview results
questions.evidence: And I'll present the interview results
questions.explain_vi: Ben trình bày kết quả phỏng vấn vì đã làm phần lớn các cuộc phỏng vấn → B.

questions.text: prepare the slides
questions.evidence: We'll prepare the slides together
questions.explain_vi: 'together' → C (cả hai).

questions.text: ask permission to use photos
questions.evidence: Clara's going to contact the garden coordinators to ask permission to use their photos.
questions.explain_vi: Ben nói Clara sẽ liên hệ xin phép → A. Chú ý: người nói là Ben nhưng người làm là Clara.

questions.text: write the conclusion
questions.evidence: Ben's going to write that.
questions.explain_vi: Clara nói Ben sẽ viết kết luận → B.

parts.title: Part 4
parts.heading: The history of chocolate
parts.context: A lecturer is giving a talk about the history of chocolate.
script: Good morning. Today we're looking at the history of chocolate, a product that has changed remarkably over the centuries.
Chocolate comes from the seeds of the cacao tree, which grows only in hot, wet regions close to the equator. The tree was first cultivated in Central America more than three thousand years ago.

For the Maya and later the Aztecs, chocolate was not a sweet food but a bitter drink. The seeds were roasted, ground and mixed with water, maize and chilli. It was often drunk at religious ceremonies and weddings.
Cacao seeds were so valuable that the Aztecs used them as money. A rabbit, for example, cost about ten seeds, and taxes could be paid in cacao.

When the Spanish arrived in the sixteenth century, they found the drink too bitter. Back in Spain, they began adding sugar and cinnamon, and the sweetened drink became fashionable among the wealthy. For about a century, the Spanish managed to keep the recipe a secret from the rest of Europe.

By the seventeenth century, chocolate houses had opened in London, where wealthy men met to drink chocolate, discuss politics and do business. Chocolate was still very expensive, mainly because of high taxes on imported cacao.

The great change came with industrial machinery. In 1828, a Dutch chemist invented a press that separated cocoa butter from the rest of the bean, leaving a powder that was much easier to mix with liquids. This invention made chocolate cheaper and led, in 1847, to the first chocolate bar, made by a British company.
Later in the nineteenth century, Swiss manufacturers added a new ingredient: condensed milk. Milk chocolate was smoother and sweeter, and it quickly became more popular than dark chocolate.

Today, most of the world's cacao is grown not in the Americas but in West Africa, especially in Ivory Coast and Ghana. Many of the farmers are poor and receive only a small share of the price of a chocolate bar, which has led to the growth of fair trade schemes that guarantee them a minimum price.

questions.explain_vi: 'water, maize and chilli' → chilli (ớt). Chấp nhận cả cách viết chili.

questions.text: The Aztecs used cacao seeds as ___.
questions.evidence: the Aztecs used them as money
questions.explain_vi: 'used them as money' → money.

questions.text: In Spain, sugar and ___ were added to the drink.
questions.evidence: they began adding sugar and cinnamon
questions.explain_vi: 'sugar and cinnamon' → cinnamon (quế).

questions.text: The Spanish kept the recipe ___ for about a hundred years.
questions.evidence: the Spanish managed to keep the recipe a secret from the rest of Europe
questions.explain_vi: 'keep the recipe a secret' → secret.

questions.text: In London chocolate houses, men talked about politics and ___.
questions.evidence: discuss politics and do business
questions.explain_vi: 'discuss politics and do business' → business.

questions.text: Chocolate was expensive mainly because of high ___.
questions.evidence: mainly because of high taxes on imported cacao
questions.explain_vi: 'high taxes on imported cacao' → taxes.

questions.text: In 1828, a ___ separated cocoa butter from the bean.
questions.evidence: a Dutch chemist invented a press that separated cocoa butter
questions.explain_vi: 'invented a press' → press (máy ép).

questions.text: Swiss makers added condensed ___ to make a smoother chocolate.
questions.evidence: Swiss manufacturers added a new ingredient: condensed milk
questions.explain_vi: 'condensed milk' → milk.

questions.text: Today most cacao is grown in West ___.
questions.evidence: most of the world's cacao is grown not in the Americas but in West Africa
